market_holds: The options hold a large move: the front (11-20) straddle prices 14.05%, 13.68% net of ordinary vol, with ATM IV 168.8% and skew slightly toward calls (25d put minus call -3.3 vol pts) (sealed baseline, 2026-11-17 18:08 UTC). GLBE's own reactions measured to about 13:00 ET (my hourly-bar arithmetic, Yahoo bars) have a median absolute size near 9% and are mostly down: 2024-11 +10.9, 2025-02 -15.2, 2025-05 -16.3, 2025-08 -7.2, 2025-11 -7.5, 2026-02 +14.3, 2026-05 -5.7, 2026-08 -2.7. The last two were beat-and-raise prints that popped premarket (+7% and +15% at the high) and were negative by midday. Spot is $40.18, -10.5% from the 52-week high. Run-in: -3.8% over 20d against QQQ about -10% and SHOP -17%, and -4.3% over 5d against QQQ -3%. So the stock has shown relative strength into the print rather than run up on its own news. Its +8.3% on 11-04 came with SHOP's +7.3% bounce after Shopify's results. Consensus Q3 revenue is about $312.6M on Yahoo (11 analysts, $310.0-315.2M) and $314.8M on Earnings Whispers (preview of 2026-11-10). Both sit inside the guide of $308.5-315.5M, near its top. EPS is about $0.33 against a $0.35 whisper. FY revenue consensus is about $1.34B (TIKR) against a guide of $1.305-1.355B, which implies roughly $474M for Q4. Short interest is low at 2.5% of float. The preview says the stock trades on beating the top of the range plus another FY raise (fourth in a row), with gross margin and take rate watched.
view: A beat on Q3 revenue and GMV is close to certain and is already the base case. GLBE has landed at or above the top of its range every quarter: Q3'25 at or above the top, Q1'26 GMV $1.74B against a $1.705-1.745B guide, and Q2'26 GMV $2.089B against $1.95-1.99B. The Q3 GMV guide implies only 32-35% growth on Q3'25's $1.51B, against 44% in Q2. Consensus sits inside the range, so the headline will read as a beat, and the market knows that pattern. The reaction turns on the Q4/FY guide and the gross-margin and take-rate story. On those, the data that arrived since 2026-08-12 leans mildly against. Shopify (Q3, 2026-11-03) slowed: GMV +29% against +32% in Q2, international GMV +32% against +37%, and GMV missed by about 0.8%. The euro has fallen from a 1.159 August average (when the guide was set) to 1.103 on 2026-11-13, about -5%, and the broad dollar index is at its highest of the year. That is a headwind to USD-reported Q4 GMV against an implied Q4 consensus of about +41% revenue growth (including Passport). The company also attributed Q2's overshoot partly to promotional activity. Against all that, Adobe forecasts US holiday online sales +6.7%, the company is still guiding conservatively, FY consensus is only at the guide midpoint, and the multiple is low for its history. The stock's habit of fading premarket strength into midday is the most consistent thing in its record, and the window ends at 13:00 ET. Overall I lean slightly down, but nothing here is sharp enough to say the price is wrong. A 13.7% implied move already covers a wide range of outcomes.

recommendation.reason: No mechanism clears 65%. The Q3 beat is the known base case. The negatives (Shopify's international slowdown, the euro's ~5% drop since the guide was set, the fade-into-midday habit) are modest and partly visible to anyone who watches Shopify and FX. The Q4/FY guide could still be raised by the size of the Q3 beat, as in every prior quarter.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 GMV well above $2.10B (organic growth near 40%+) together with a FY GMV raise of more than the Q3 beat, and steady gross margin, would make the up case likely.

self_critique: GLBE has beaten and raised in every quarter of 2025-26, and the consensus FY revenue only sits at the guide midpoint. A Q3 GMV above $2.1B with a FY raise could carry the stock with the reported 15% premarket pops, as in Feb 2026. The fade pattern is 8 observations and may just reflect the tape on those days. FX volatility can lift GLBE's FX-conversion revenue, and the dollar's move may be small against its merchant mix. Shopify still grew ~30%, and GLBE has grown faster than Shopify for years. So the lean down is weak.
approach_notes: P6 (take apart the run-in, find the line) and the 'freshest data first' rule helped: Shopify's results and the FX move are the post-call data. P4's warning made me keep the FX and Shopify signals small, since I cannot show the consensus has not absorbed them. The window rule (13:00 ET) mattered more than any fundamental, because of this name's habit of fading premarket pops.
